claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: An induced-minor sequence gives the six inverse-image branch sets, whose inter-set adjacencies agree exactly with K6 minus AB. Conversely, delete unused vertices and contract spanning trees inside the six sets; anticompleteness prevents an AB edge and the other fourteen adjacencies remain. A seven-label assignment specifies the certificate, and all conditions are testable in O(n²), yielding O(7^n n²) time and NP membership.
claims.witness: A successful seven-label assignment, with label 0 unused and six nonempty connected branch labels, is a polynomial-size certificate and contracts to exactly K6 minus AB.
claims.search_method: Direct bidirectional proof from the definition of induced minor; no external search.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: If q=0, no two nonempty sets are anticomplete. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, the endpoints of any nonedge together with those universal vertices induce the target. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices, while every other vertex is among the at most 2q endpoints of the q nonedges; hence n≤2q+3. Applying claim 0 gives the stated FPT time. For q≤C log n, 7^(2q+3) is polynomial in n.
claims.witness: For any nonedge xy and four universal vertices u1,…,u4, G[{x,y,u1,…,u4}] is exactly K6 minus xy.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive case split on q and the number of universal vertices; no external search.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: In the subgraph induced by a model, the t−2 core branches give t−2 internally disjoint A–B paths, so any A–B separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least t−2. An inclusion-minimal such separator S is a clique in a chordal graph: two nonadjacent members, joined by shortest paths through the two full sides, would form a chordless cycle. Each full component contains an S-complete vertex. Indeed, maximize its S-neighborhood; a shortest path to a neighbor of a missed s∈S, together with chordality, forces the terminal vertex to retain all previous S-neighbors and gain s. Taking S-complete vertices x and y from the two sides and any t−2 vertices of S induces Kt minus xy. The reverse implication is immediate, and enumeration gives O(n^6) for t=6.
claims.witness: The induced witness is {x,y}∪S0, where S0 is any (t−2)-subset of the clique separator S; x and y are nonadjacent and complete to S0.
claims.search_method: Independent minimal-separator proof, including the full-component lemma; no external search.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: Anticompleteness forces both exceptional branches into one independent part i, and connectivity makes each a singleton. A core is either a singleton in a distinct outside part or spans at least two parts. Every spanning core can be reduced to a cross-part edge without losing any required adjacency: such an edge meets both exceptional vertices, every outside singleton, and every other cross-part edge. Thus the remaining cores are precisely a matching after reserving the exceptional and singleton-core vertices. Any matching has size at most both ⌊M/2⌋ and M−L; pairing vertices from different largest remaining parts attains their minimum. Enumerating i, s, and J is polynomial.
claims.witness: Two reserved vertices in part i, singleton cores in the parts J, and 4−s disjoint residual cross-part edges form a model exactly when the stated test accepts.
claims.search_method: Structural normalization proof plus exhaustive finite verification of the matching formula on all count vectors with at most five parts and total at most eleven.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: A nice-decomposition DP can store the seven-way label of each bag vertex, the connectivity partition for every branch label, unseen/active/closed flags, and fourteen required-adjacency bits. Forgetting the last boundary vertex of a nonfinal component is rejected because the decomposition separator prevents later reconnection; closed labels cannot reappear. Introduce-edge nodes merge same-label components, record required adjacencies, and reject AB edges. Compatible join states combine partitions by transitive closure and union their edge bits while excluding disconnected off-bag copies. The empty-root condition is equivalent to a valid model. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a target-dependent constant states; even quadratic join pairing remains 2^{O(w log w)}.
claims.witness: An accepting empty-root state has all six labels closed exactly once, every label connected, all fourteen required bits set, and no AB edge.
claims.search_method: Independent invariant and state-count audit of the proposed tree-decomposition dynamic program; no external search.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two paths and four singleton ci form the displayed model. A singleton exceptional vertex needs four distinct neighbors, so it must be some ci. Its anticomplete exceptional partner is a connected interval in one component of A−ai or B−bi. Exhaustive enumeration shows that c2 and c3 permit no such interval with four external neighbors. For c1 and c4, the only viable intervals have exactly four boundary vertices, one of which is isolated after deleting the two exceptional branches. The four core branches would have to use the four boundary vertices separately, making the branch containing that isolated vertex anticomplete to the other cores, a contradiction.
claims.witness: A={a1,a2,a3,a4}, B={b1,b2,b3,b4}, and Cj={cj} give a valid model, while the finite singleton analysis excludes every alternative model with a singleton exceptional branch.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of every degree-eligible singleton and every connected anticomplete partner subset in the specified 12-vertex graph.

claims.claim: In every subcubic graph, each exceptional branch set in a K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor model has at least two vertices and each of the four core branch sets has at least three vertices. Consequently every such model uses at least 16 vertices.
claims.evidence: For a connected k-vertex set S in a subcubic graph, |δ(S)|=Σdeg(v)−2|E(S)|≤3k−2(k−1)=k+2. An exceptional branch needs boundary edges to four distinct core branches, so k+2≥4 and k≥2. A core branch needs boundary edges to the other five branches, so k+2≥5 and k≥3. Disjointness then gives at least 2+2+4·3=16 vertices.
claims.witness: The boundary requirements are four for each exceptional branch and five for each core branch; substituting them into |δ(S)|≤|S|+2 yields the six stated lower bounds.
claims.search_method: Direct exact degree-sum and connectivity argument; no external search.

claims.claim: The subcubic lower bound is tight: the following 16-vertex cubic graph contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor. Its six branch paths are A=a1a2, B=b1b2, and Ci=ci1ci2ci3 for i=1,…,4. Besides the path edges, add a1c11,a1c21,a2c31,a2c41, b1c11,b1c21,b2c31,b2c41, c12c22,c32c42,c13c33,c13c43,c23c33,c23c43, and no other edges.
claims.evidence: Exact reconstruction gives 16 vertices, 24 edges, and degree three at every vertex. The six listed sets are disjoint connected paths; A and B have no cross-edge. The first eight added edges realize all A/B-to-core adjacencies, and the last six realize the six core-pair adjacencies exactly once. Hence they form a valid induced-minor model, meeting claim 6's lower bound.
claims.witness: The branch partition A, B, C1,…,C4 specified in the claim is a valid spanning model in the reconstructed cubic graph.
claims.search_method: Exact graph reconstruction, degree count, and all fifteen branch-pair adjacency checks.

claims.claim: For ℓ≥1, let Xℓ be obtained by replacing every edge of the preceding 16-vertex cubic graph by a path of ℓ edges. Then Xℓ is connected and bridgeless, has 24ℓ−8 vertices, 24ℓ edges, maximum degree 3, cycle rank 9, and treewidth exactly 4, and contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor.
claims.evidence: Uniform subdivision gives 16+24(ℓ−1)=24ℓ−8 vertices and 24ℓ edges, so connectedness gives cycle rank 24ℓ−(24ℓ−8)+1=9. Exact checking confirms every base edge lies on a cycle; subdivision therefore preserves bridgelessness and maximum degree three. Contracting subdivision paths recovers the base induced minor. The displayed base elimination order has maximum filled later-degree four, and subdivision vertices can first be eliminated with later-degree two. Conversely, K6 minus an edge is an ordinary minor and has treewidth four, proving equality.
claims.witness: Assign each subdivision-path interior to one endpoint's original branch set; the six expanded sets form a valid model. Eliminating all subdivision interiors and then using the stated base order has width four.
claims.search_method: Symbolic counting and minor arguments, supplemented by exact checks for ℓ=1,…,6, including connectivity, every-edge deletion, model validity, cycle rank, and elimination width.

claims.claim: Every K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor model in Xℓ is spanning. Consequently its largest branch set has at least 4ℓ−1 vertices. Thus branch-set size is unbounded even for subcubic hosts of the minimum possible maximum degree and treewidth.
claims.evidence: For a model union U, Xℓ[U] is connected and contracts to the target. Contraction and deletion of loops or parallel edges cannot increase binary cycle-space dimension, so its dimension is at least the target's 14−6+1=9. Its cycle space embeds into the nine-dimensional cycle space of Xℓ. If U omitted a vertex v, bridgelessness supplies a cycle through v; its vector has an edge outside Xℓ[U], proving the embedded subspace proper and hence of dimension at most eight, a contradiction. Thus U is spanning. Averaging 24ℓ−8 vertices over six branches gives ceiling (24ℓ−8)/6=4ℓ−1. Maximum degree two is impossible by the boundary inequality, and treewidth below four is impossible because the target is a minor.
claims.witness: For any hypothetical omitted vertex v, a cycle through v is a cycle-space vector outside the embedded cycle space of Xℓ[U], contradicting the required dimension nine.
claims.search_method: Independent binary cycle-space proof; the persisted checker verifies all graph premises and arithmetic for ℓ=1,…,6.

claims.claim: For every integer ℓ≥1, let Fℓ consist of a clique Q={c0,c1,c2,c3}, two mutually anticomplete induced paths a0…a(3ℓ) and b0…b(3ℓ), and, besides the clique and path edges, exactly the edges ci-a(iℓ) and ci-b(iℓ) for i=0,1,2,3. Then Fℓ has maximum degree 5 and treewidth exactly 4, and it contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor.
claims.evidence: Each ci has its three clique edges and two attachment edges, while path vertices have degree at most three, so the maximum is exactly five. The two full paths and the four singleton ci form a model. Eliminating either path from one end propagates only the already passed clique attachments: each eliminated vertex has at most its successor and four clique vertices as later neighbors, with the endpoint having no successor; the maximum is four. After both paths, Q has width three. Thus treewidth is at most four, while the target ordinary minor has treewidth four, giving equality.
claims.witness: The full a-path, full b-path, and singleton sets {c0},…,{c3} form the induced-minor model; the stated path-first elimination order has width four.
claims.search_method: Direct degree/model proof plus exact elimination simulation for ℓ=1,…,8.

claims.claim: In Fℓ, the minimum, over all K6-minus-an-edge induced-minor models, of max(|A|,|B|) for the two exceptional nonadjacent branch sets is exactly ℓ+1. Consequently no constant depending only on the target can bound both exceptional branch sets, even on hosts of maximum degree 5 and the minimum possible treewidth 4.
claims.evidence: Because Q is a clique, at least one exceptional branch S avoids Q. Connectivity then makes S an interval in one of the two path components of Fℓ−Q. If it contains r attachment sites, its boundary has at most r attachment edges plus two path-boundary edges. Four distinct core adjacencies require at least four boundary edges, so r≥2. Consecutive attachment sites are ℓ edges apart, hence |S|≥ℓ+1 and max(|A|,|B|)≥ℓ+1. The two middle intervals of length ℓ+1, singleton cores c1,c2, and prefix/suffix cores containing c0,c3 respectively realize equality exactly as claimed.
claims.witness: Take A={aj:ℓ≤j≤2ℓ}, B={bj:ℓ≤j≤2ℓ}, the singleton cores {c1},{c2}, and the connected prefix and suffix cores containing c0 and c3. Both exceptional branches have size ℓ+1.
claims.search_method: Universal boundary argument plus exact validation of every path interval and the equality model for ℓ=1,…,8.
